text:
maria: Quick question — while testing the new inference rollout I hit two weird behaviors with the generation endpoint: (1) stop sequences seem to be ignored in some low max_tokens cases, and (2) enabling `logprobs` changes where truncation happens. Anyone seen this?

kevin: what model + payload? stop as string or array? temp/top_p set?

maria: repro payload:
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-alpha-7b",
  "prompt": "Write a haiku about clouds",
  "max_tokens": 3,
  "temperature": 0.7,
  "top_p": 1.0,
  "stop": ["\n\n"],
  "logprobs": 5
}
```
Expected: generator returns fewer tokens and honors stop. Observed: sometimes returns 3 tokens but the stop sequence appears inside tokenization so stop wasn't applied; other times with `logprobs` set we get partial tokens and `choices[0].finish_reason` = "length" even though stop matched.

leo: I vaguely remember tokenizer boundary issues — stop strings that cross token boundaries need special handling. Also `logprobs` forces a sampling branch that may return early for performance reasons.

ashley: is this a breaking contract change? product needs to know if customers will see different outputs after the rollout.

kevin: not expected to be breaking. Looks like a bug in how stop-checks interact with the sampling path. PR in flight: https://internal/repo/pull/2345 (fixes stop check + adds tests)

dev-bot: CI passed for PR #2345 on main :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks — can we get a short checklist of regression cases before we merge? I'll add them to the rollout playbook.

kevin: proposed checklist (quick):
1) stop as string vs array
2) stop that spans token boundary
3) max_tokens < length to stop
4) with/without `logprobs`
5) temp=0 vs temp>0 vs top_p<1
6) finish_reason values (stop / length / eos)

samir: I'll run regtests today. Command I'll use:
`./bin/run-regtests --suite gen-stop --jobs 8 --record` 
I'll attach logs here.

maria: also add a canary plan: 5% traffic on dedicated -> monitor finish_reason distribution + token histograms for 24h.

ashley: if there's any customer-facing change we should gate behind a feature flag. Suggest `compat.stop_legacy_behavior=true` defaulting to current behavior for two releases.

kevin: we can do that. Implementation note: avoid adding a second control path in runtime — instead add a shim in the API layer that transforms requests when flag is on. That keeps runtime efficient.

leo: quick code review note — watch out for double counting tokens when we run a stop-match fallback after KV-cache reuse. I added a comment on the PR.

maria: can someone @me when PR merges? I'll prep release notes and the playbook entries.

kevin: ping me for review — I can approve after the added tests. cc @samir for the regression run.

samir: started regtests, will paste results in ~30m.

maria: perfect, thanks all :thumbsup:
